text:
Sam: Quick brain dump: I think we can avoid per-prefix heavy metadata by propagating tombstone summaries as a compact bloom / delta stream. Idea: each node publishes a bloom of recently deleted prefixes (time-windowed).
Priya: Bloom sounds promising for scale. How do we handle false positives? They'd cause extra revalidations but that's acceptable if bounded.
Omar: Two main concerns: (1) false positive rate tuning vs bandwidth, (2) how to guarantee not to miss a deletion (false negative).
Sam: Right. Use conservative parameters to avoid false negatives (bloom never false negative if constructed correctly). We might also send a tiny periodic exact tail for hot prefixes to clear up false positives.
Lin: What's the hit-path change? On cache hit we currently trust local entry. With bloom, we have to check bloom membership for prefix; if bloom says "maybe deleted" then revalidate against store.
Priya: That adds a bloom lookup per hit. Bloom lookup is cheap (few hashes). Should be fine for p95.
Omar: How do we disseminate blooms? Full mesh pub/sub is heavy. Use membership stream with epoch ids; nodes subscribe and apply XOR-merge of recent blooms for their region.
Sam: Proposal: each node emits per-shard bloom for tombstones with TTL window T. Nodes maintain sliding-window aggregate bloom = OR of blooms in last N windows. On a hit, check aggregate bloom.
Lin: OR-aggregates increase false positives over time. Need to bound N and T. Also consider rotating salt per window to reduce correlation attacks.
Priya: For strict mode tenants we can fall back to exact metadata: write deletion into a tiny consensus-backed metadata table. Default is bloom mode.
Omar: What about partitioning? If a node is partitioned and misses a deletion emission, it may serve stale unless its local cache has tombstone. But we already have that risk.
Sam: To mitigate, when we receive a remote write/handshake (lease handoff, etc.) include recent bloom digest/prefix-epoch vector so nodes learn deletions opportunistically.
Lin: Tests: fuzz cross-node deletes + bloom false positive/negative injection, ensure false negatives are zero, measure extra revalidations due to false positives.
Priya: Metrics: bloom size per-node, aggregate false-positive rate, revalidate-per-sec, stale-serve incidents.
Omar: Implementation notes: pick murmur3 or highwayhash and 3-4 hash funcs. Keep bloom word size per-shard configurable.
Sam: Ops: need rollout plan to avoid sudden revalidation spikes. Start with conservative tiny bloom window, monitor revalidate rate, then tune.
kv-bot: deploybot: rolling canary queued for tombstone-bloom-bridge branch.
